title: Ab Interno vs. Ab Externo Microcatheter-Assisted Circumferential Trabeculotomy in Treating Patients With Primary Open-Angle Glaucoma

license.statement: CC BY (article <license>: 'Creative Commons Attribution License (CC BY)'; no version number or licence URL given in the XML)

indication: primary open-angle glaucoma (mean age about 35 years) with uncontrolled IOP, progressive visual field loss on maximum medication or medication intolerance; about half of the eyes had prior failed filtration surgery (trabeculectomy, Ex-PRESS, Ahmed); one eye per patient; retrospective comparative case series, single surgeon (Beijing Tongren, China)

groups.description: Group 1: microcatheter-assisted (iTrack) ab interno circumferential trabeculotomy through a 1-2 mm nasal goniotomy (GATT-type); 40 eyes of 40 patients (T1!R2C2)

Group 2: microcatheter-assisted ab externo circumferential trabeculotomy via a superficial scleral flap and scleral cut-down into Schlemm's canal; 54 eyes of 54 patients (T1!R2C3); classed 'angle_mims' as an angle (trabeculotomy) procedure like canaloplasty in the protocol list

exclusions.reason: medication numbers are not IOP series in schema 1.0.0; noted only

exclusions.reason: figure-only; the text gives only percent reductions without the subgroup reference IOP

exclusions.what: percent IOP reduction and medication reduction (text)
exclusions.reason: changes reported in text without tabulated per-visit values; absolute series used
success proportions / Kaplan-Meier estimates are not admissible

notes: Reference kind 'preoperative_medicated': patients had uncontrolled IOP or progression on maximum medication (or intolerance), and the preoperative number of medications is tabulated (T1!R14C2, T1!R14C3); no washout described.
Tonometer not stated in the article, so method 'unstated'.

Postoperative pilocarpine 2% four times daily for 3 months was part of standard care and not counted as anti-glaucoma medication by the authors; IOP elevations in the first month were treated only above 25 mmHg; anterior chamber irrigation for massive hyphema with IOP spike.
Seven patients lost to follow-up after the first week were not included in the analysed 94 eyes (ordinary attrition, not outcome-defined).
Both arms are standard circumferential trabeculotomy approaches compared without an investigational agent, so both are 'control' groups.
